items.title: Tom Stagg Interview, 1969-10-03
items.q: Every now and again when the Kenny Ball or the Chris Barber Band or the Ackerbilt Band are back in England, they'll do one job at the 100 Club while they're in passing through.

ctx.x: about six or eight of them, they had about five records between them. And they had written and asked me, in fact, if they could have Chic and Handy, but they'd left it so late it was impossible to organise anything with Chic and Handy, but we said the next musician we bring to England, we would offer them. We offered them Lewis Nelson, and they jumped at the idea. So we flew with Nelson to Milan. Now Lewis Nelson was the first New Orleans musician ever to go to Italy. And it has worked out today that he's paved…

And this is really sad for England because to us we've gone down a stage. We got to a very good period where British traditional style bands were playing concerts. And big jobs, the Royal Festival Hall, the Conway Hall, which we've already mentioned. The Royal Festival Hall has symphony concerts and symphony orchestras. And the British traditional bands got to this stage where they were playing this type of job. And we now feel as if we've gone down a stage. That the English bands are now playing these pub jobs…
